title: Pull-ups are GARBAGE for LATS (according to biomechanics
summary: Reaction to a biomechanics guru's post claiming pull-ups are poor for lat growth. NH debunks each argument (arm not tight to body, humerus not moving backward, internal rotation, lat disengaged at bottom) with grip and technique fixes, and argues from empirical evidence (calisthenics athletes, climbers, natural lifters) that weighted pull-ups beat cable isolation for building lats.
claims: Pull-ups are essential for a complete back as a natural lifter; NH went from poor lats to decent lats with pull-ups only
Critics of classic lifts are usually either skinny guys with a physio degree or enhanced big guys telling you compounds don't work
Biomechanics gurus always replace a hard classic lift with an easier gimmick, e.g. swapping deadlifts for lying leg curls done for sets of 15
Claiming pull-ups build rear delts and traps more than lats is nonsense; calisthenics athletes are not known for huge upper traps
If a wide grip keeps the arm too far from the body, just bring the grip in; chin-ups and neutral grip keep arms close and many feel lats more on chin-ups
Rotate the arm outward and put pressure on the pinky fingers during pull-ups to bring the elbow closer to the body, force external rotation and recruit the lats
The humerus moves down rather than back in a pull-up because of gravity, but as long as you pull against gravity the lats are worked
Most criticism of big compound lifts targets a specific bad execution; the beauty of compounds is you can rearrange your body around the bar to fix it
Going into a dead hang at the bottom disengages the shoulders and lats; cut the range of motion short to keep constant tension on the lats
You fix a lift pattern rather than throwing the lift away because some people do it badly

Exercise intensity has an internal component (within a lift) and a cross component (lift vs lift); a weighted pull-up is more intense than a one-arm cable row, so it should sit higher in the priority pyramid for lat size
Pro bodybuilders replacing rows and pull-ups with light high-rep cable work only works because they are on drugs; it does not work for naturals
Cable rows are fine to finish the lats, not as the main stimulus; naturals need heavy, more destructive movements
NH built his lats strictly with pull-ups and pullovers, the only two lat lifts available in his home gym, proving lifts without a tight arm work
Science-based gurus rely on EMG data and ignore real-world empirical evidence, cherry-picking data to fit their agenda
Nearly all natural bodybuilders with big lats and upper backs built them with pull-ups and vertical pulls, from the bronze era to today
Calisthenics athletes and climbers have some of the best backs of any athletes because they constantly do pull-up motions
Claiming only genetically gifted people grow lats with pull-ups is a built-in excuse that weaponizes genetics against any counter-example
Almost anyone who did weighted pull-ups would see massive lat growth
A generation following isolation-cable advice will be a generation of small lifters; build big muscles with heavy compounds
exercises: rotate arms outward, pressure on pinky fingers, avoid dead hang, keep lats loaded
